title: Web research report

upstream.role: requirement source; no upstream code copied

notes: Extracted from the evaluator of the paper's final Creation evaluation with the Lite delta (provider constants, Builder session-limit freeze, n_concurrent 1-2) and the release edits; verify_score fatal filter includes 'dimensions must be an object' (Lite fix).

The trusted independent-source fetcher (benchmark/evaluator/independent_sources.py, run on the host at staging) reads PDFs with the QA environment's Python, as in the paper; setup therefore builds both envs.

Runnable with deepseek-flash for every role on the DeepSeek API (smoke-default Creation runtime effort none, Builder and judge effort max). A smoke runs end to end: the Builder froze (builder_exit); its candidate searched 466 times through the per-run search front with the read-only trust mounts staged (broker accounting 466/466 HTTP 200); held-out test_001 reached the Result judge (1 call, no failure): scoreable, contract valid, score publishable, score 0, a candidate-quality zero (the judge's validity rule: the report was an unfocused excerpt dump, not the requested decision report); both dev cases were candidate timeouts at 600 s. Earlier smokes, before the read-only trust mounts were added, scored dev_001 = 62 and dev_002 = 76 (scoreable, valid, publishable; 2 judge calls; 239/239 searches through the front) and held-out test_001 = 25 (valid, publishable). The shared add_search_front path is also covered by a PPTX smoke (8 trust mounts staged, 7/7 searches) and by tests/e2e_search_front.py (19/19). Candidate-quality zeros stay common with the flash Builder: a candidate that reads SERPER_TOKEN only from its process environment, which the evaluator's Web candidate runner does not set, never loads the documented credential file and searches nothing.

Release change (2026-10-10): adapter/eval-template/solution/run_eval.py normalize_evaluation_state reads the judge's prose (assessment, major_errors) as an infrastructure marker only when it holds the standalone token INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR or INFRASTRUCTURE_INVALID (underscores, any case, no letter, digit or underscore immediately before or after). The previous rule turned every non-alphanumeric into '_' and matched substrings, so prose such as 'evaluator-side infrastructure errors' voided a scored case. The harness, the transport and the judge's structured evaluation_state mark infrastructure as before, and verify_score.py reads the state run_eval writes.

Release change (2026-10-11): adapter/eval-template/solution/run_eval.py retries a Result-judge request once with reduced evidence when it does not fit the judge context, as the repository-bug-repair and database-analytics evals do. The trigger is an HTTP 400 whose body says the context length was exceeded, or an HTTP 400 with no provider message while the prompt's upper token estimate is above 900,000 (the 1,048,576-token context minus the 100,000-token output limit, less 5%). The first request is unchanged. The reduced prompt is built in steps, re-estimated after each, and the eval stops once it fits: repeated harness values become references, then binary files, then files that are neither required deliverables (report.md, sources.json, evidence_graph.json, run_report.json) nor listed in run_report.json artifacts (the optional diagnostics/ directory, which is not evaluated, for example), become path/size/sha256 markers. The trusted images go with both requests unchanged and count toward the estimate. A case the deterministic gate settles still gets no judge request. A prompt that still does not fit, or a failed retry, stays an infrastructure error. eval_result.json records evidence_reduced, a non-scoring prompt_reduction receipt (also prompt_reduction.json) and redacted samples of every judge 4xx body (judge_http_errors). verify_score.py is unchanged.
